What Are the Advantages of Prefab Houses?

2024-06-06

Prefabricated houses are modular houses that are crafted in factories and later moved and erected on-site. These houses are important constituents in American housing society, and they are valued for the perks they come with. Not only can you save up to 50% of the cost that you could have invested in less than a similar-sized site-built home. Wondering what are the other advantages of prefab houses and why you should get one? Hop inside this ultimate guide to find out!

✔Reduced Construction Span

Prefab homes have shorter construction span than that of site-built ones. For instance, the construction of a site-built house takes over three months of consecutive work that might get even longer depending on the weather conditions. In comparison, everything from the site work, production, and setup of a modular house will take a month or less. It's greatly influenced by the complexity of your multi-section units.

Moreover, the construction process won’t be affected by the weather, too. All the components will be constructed in the factory and assembled on the construction site – even the temperature below freezing point won’t affect this process. Lastly, reduced construction time means savings on construction loan interest.

✔Flexibility of Customization

Pre built homes are meant to incorporate all the personalized details one wishes to include in their house. Gone are the days when you had to believe in the notion of an off-the-shelf house. Now, you can collaborate with an architect to put all your wishes on paper and use the resulting layout for your house production. You can flexibly customize everything from color and size to the fixtures and fittings of your prefab houses.

✔Fixed Price Guarantee

According to prefabricated house manufacturer, prefabricated homes can be constructed at 50% less cost than that of site-built ones. It’s because these are constructed in a controlled indoor environment without any cost overruns due to theft of materials, weather damage to building products, subcontractor delays, vandalism, and delivery problems.

Moreover, according to data collected from industries, the labor input in prefab modular homes production is also minimal, leading to the labor cost component being 8 to 12 percent of the entire cost. On the other hand, site-built homes contribute 40 to 60 percent of the total cost.

Also, the cost of standard building materials is reduced to 30 percent of the total cost as factories purchase things in bulk. This difference can save you loads of money, especially in urban areas where labor is more expensive. So, once you have signed the contract, rest assured of having a fixed price guarantee for up to 12 months for the whole range of services.

✔Lower Average Permit Value

Though we have discussed the reduced-price thing, that doesn't account for the overall cost alone. You might think the construction cost of prefab shipping container homes are reduced, but their shipping and implantation costs overlook the price gap. That's not the case! You need to understand the concept of lower average permit value to analyze the price difference better.

This is because around 80 percent of prefab homes are customized on the owner's lot, which records the sale price. On the other hand, the site-built homes are often constructed speculatively for sale at some point in the future. According to the National Association of Home Builders, the average permit value of a site-built home is $94.34 per square foot. On the other hand, it's $76.80 for prefab ones.

✔Consistent Quality

Quality control of pre built homes are also worth mentioning. These houses are created in a sophisticated setting by professionals who excel in building houses on a daily basis. Moreover, their work is supervised by a skilled tradesperson, and they undergo continuous training. So, you can’t doubt their skills when it comes to crafting a quality house.

Moreover, certain factory operations are also subjected to state supervision under multiple programs, including independent inspection agencies. Aside from these, the technology, machinery, and tools used in their construction are also top-notch. Specific computer programs, lasers, and templates are also utilized to ensure ideal cuts and joints.

✔Ideal for Remote Locations

If you are trying to construct a site-built house in a remote location, you will know the hassle of finding a contractor willing to travel to a remote location for construction purposes. You can ditch this issue with prefab houses. As mentioned earlier, these are constructed in centralized and controlled sections of factories and can be transported to wherever you want once completed.

However, it won’t be hard to find someone to set up your pre-built house at the desired location. You may even ask your prefabricated house manufacturer for setup services. Most even provide it with the construction process.

✔Energy Efficiency

Aside from saving money during construction, you can also save money when living in these houses, as they are built to be energy efficient. Individual parts of a prefab container home adhere to strict design guidelines, resulting in airtight seams. This, in turn, ensures avoidance of leaks and airflows that have potential of increasing the economic and energetic cost of cooling or heating your house. 

Moreover, with the advancements in the construction process, prefabricated house manufacturers are also incorporating more energy-efficient elements. These can include solar panels, rainwater catchment systems, wind turbines, and more.

✔Value Retention

Another perk is the life expectancy of the prefab modular homes. Usually, it lasts for over 20 years, and it's comparable to a house that's built with conventional construction methods. It's because prefab container homes constructed nowadays are passed through rigorous testing to ensure quality control. A plethora of factors are considered throughout the process of construction and assembly.

This, in turn, ensures a 20-year life expectancy, assuming proper construction. However, it may vary depending on the maintenance and care. So, once you have one, be sure to maintain it well.

✔Minimal Waste

To your surprise, one-quarter of all the non-industry waste in the U.S. is produced by the demolition and construction industries. That said, all the construction processes nowadays are focused on greater production efficiency, resulting in minimal waste. The same is the case with the modular house production. Since these are constructed within the factory, the reusage of leftover materials increases significantly.

Moreover, the construction material for prefab shipping container homes isn't prone to theft, which is a great threat to site-built homes. This can save you from lots of hassle, as prefab house construction requires 10 to 30 percent more materials. The more materials you add, the more durable your house will be.

✔Safety

Note that the building material used in the modular houses’ construction is the same as that of site-built homes. Additionally, modular houses are considered safer, as these are engineered for energy efficiency and wind safety based on the geographic region in which they are sold.

Prefab container house’ safety is also ensured by the fact that they are subjected to several federal laws for the inclusion of certain security features. These include at least two exterior doors, smoke detectors, egress windows in bedrooms, standards on smoke generation in materials, and limited combustible materials around water heaters, furnaces, and kitchen ranges.

Where to Source Prefab Houses?

By now, you must have thought about investing in prefab container house. If that’s the case, we recommend checking out NEW BRAND. This amazing construction company excels in offering an array of prefab shipping container homes. From expandable container houses and detachable ones to folding ones, capsule houses, and more – they have it all.  

The best part about them is their business philosophy: honesty, quality, joint development, and achieving win-win results. Moreover, their customer service is also a cherry on top. Want to have more details? Hop onto their website!

Wrapping It Up!

Prefab houses might seem more expensive and hassle-causing than those of prefab modular homes, but that's not actually the case. Not only do these offer reduced construction costs and Average Permit Value, but they also ensure minimal waste, energy efficiency, and other such perks. So, getting them can never be a bad idea.
